transcript: It is the 25th anniversary of 9/11. So obviously, we're watching Come From Away. I love this musical so much. But one of the reasons why I think it's one of the best musicals written in maybe the last 20 years is the opening and how they do not reveal that it is 9/11 for the first 11 minutes of this musical. You go through an entire opening number where you know something has happened, but not exactly what. They talk about things that they need to do. Like, they know that they need to do a specific task, but they do not drop that date for the first 11 minutes of this musical. Because as soon as they do that, everybody who knows any bit of history or was alive during that time knows exactly what happened. And these characters in this moment do not know. And in writing the opening of this musical that way, they have so perfectly captured what the feeling was like that morning. Because you were going about your Tuesday like any other freaking Tuesday. And then at some point that morning, somebody somewhere told you something was happening. You did not have all of the information. You just knew something bad was happening. And everybody that was alive during that time that has memories, remembers who told them and where they were. And you. You hear that a lot, but I. It's true. It's true. I was a sixth grader in Colorado. And I know exactly where I was when I found out. I know exactly who told me when I found out. And they captured that so perfectly in this musical with this opening number. Somebody somewhere told you to turn on the radio and you were here at the start of a moment like, it doesn't. It doesn't get more accurate than that. And the way that they were able to capture that feeling so perfectly for audiences that were not alive when the events of 9/11 took place already and in the future, I think that's beautiful. That's. That is what theatre is all about, right? It's about capturing a moment in time and also showcasing what the world could be. And I think this is humanity at its best. And I. I love that. I love that about it. Anyway, this is your sign to go watch come from away. It is currently on Apple TV. Streaming. Or you can go see it at your local regional theatre, because, like, every regional theatre in the country is doing it this year for the 25th anniversary.
